_meta.notes: Maps NASA Exoplanet Archive column names to display info. Use `category` to group fields in detail views/tooltips. `precision` is a suggested decimal-place count for display. `nullLabel` is what to show when the value is missing. `siConversion` (where present) drives the hover-icon tooltip: multiply the raw archive value by `multiplier` to get the SI value in `unit`. Use `useScientificNotation: true` to format as e.g. 1.52e7 rather than a long decimal string — astronomical SI values are usually too large/small to read as plain decimals. Fields without a `siConversion` are either already in a base-ish unit (K, degrees, dimensionless) or non-physical (names, flags, counts), so no SI toggle applies. `errorFields` (where present) points to the archive's asymmetric-uncertainty columns for that measurement — `upper` is the field holding the positive (+) error, `lower` holds the negative (−) error. Per archive convention the raw lower-error value is stored as a negative number; display code should take its absolute value.

pl_name.label: Planet Name
pl_name.tooltip: Official designation, usually the host star name plus a letter (e.g. Kepler-22 b).

sy_pnum.label: Planets in System
sy_pnum.tooltip: Number of known planets orbiting the same host star.

sy_snum.label: Stars in System
sy_snum.tooltip: Number of stars in the system (1 = single star, 2+ = binary/multiple star system).

discoverymethod.label: Discovery Method
discoverymethod.tooltip: How the planet was detected — e.g. Transit (dimming starlight), Radial Velocity (stellar wobble), Direct Imaging, Microlensing.

disc_facility.label: Discovery Facility
disc_facility.tooltip: Observatory or mission that made the discovery (e.g. Kepler, TESS, K2, various ground-based telescopes).

pl_orbper.label: Orbital Period
pl_orbper.tooltip: Time for one full orbit around its star — the planet's 'year'.

pl_orbsmax.label: Orbit Distance
pl_orbsmax.tooltip: Average distance from the planet to its star, in Astronomical Units (1 AU = Earth-Sun distance).

pl_orbeccen.label: Orbital Eccentricity
pl_orbeccen.tooltip: How elliptical the orbit is. 0 = perfectly circular, closer to 1 = highly elongated.

pl_rade.label: Radius
pl_rade.tooltip: Planet's radius compared to Earth (1.0 = same size as Earth).

pl_bmasse.label: Mass
pl_bmasse.tooltip: Best-available planet mass compared to Earth (1.0 = same mass as Earth). 'Best' means the archive's preferred value where multiple measurement types exist (true mass or minimum mass from radial velocity).

pl_dens.label: Density
pl_dens.tooltip: Bulk density. For reference: Earth ≈ 5.5, Jupiter ≈ 1.3, water = 1.0.

pl_eqt.label: Equilibrium Temperature
pl_eqt.tooltip: Estimated surface/atmosphere temperature assuming no atmosphere effects (like greenhouse warming). A rough guide, not a measured surface temperature.

pl_insol.label: Insolation
pl_insol.tooltip: Amount of starlight the planet receives compared to Earth (1.0 = same as Earth receives from the Sun).

st_teff.label: Star Temperature
st_teff.tooltip: Effective surface temperature of the host star. Sun ≈ 5,772 K.

st_rad.label: Star Radius
st_rad.tooltip: Host star's radius compared to the Sun.

st_mass.label: Star Mass
st_mass.tooltip: Host star's mass compared to the Sun.

st_spectype.label: Spectral Type
st_spectype.tooltip: Star classification (e.g. G2V for a Sun-like star, M-dwarfs are cooler and redder).

st_met.label: Star Metallicity
st_met.tooltip: Relative abundance of elements heavier than hydrogen/helium in the star, compared to the Sun (0 = same as Sun).

sy_dist.label: Distance from Earth
sy_dist.tooltip: Distance from Earth to the system. 1 parsec ≈ 3.26 light-years.

sy_vmag.label: Apparent Brightness
sy_vmag.tooltip: How bright the host star appears from Earth. Lower numbers = brighter. Naked-eye limit is roughly 6.

ra.label: Right Ascension
ra.tooltip: Sky coordinate, the celestial equivalent of longitude.

dec.label: Declination
dec.tooltip: Sky coordinate, the celestial equivalent of latitude.

tran_flag.label: Transits Its Star
tran_flag.tooltip: Whether the planet is observed passing in front of its star from our vantage point.

pl_controv_flag.label: Disputed Detection
pl_controv_flag.tooltip: Flagged by the archive as a contested or unconfirmed detection in the literature. Worth a caution badge in the UI rather than hiding it.
